results.content: # How to ensure exactly once semantics while processing kafka messages in Apache Storm. When you read a message from Kafka, you can choose to commit before or after you do your processing (e.g. write to a database). Yes, there is something else Storm offers to ensure exactly once semantics called Trident, but it requires you to write your topology differently, and your data store has to be adapted to it so message deduplication can happen. Also just to caution you: When documentation for Storm (or Kafka) talk about exactly-once semantics, there are some assumptions made about what kind of processing you'll do. Finally if your processing fits the "read from Kafka, do computation, write to Kafka" model, you can likely get nicer semantics out of Kafka Streams than Storm, as Storm can't provide the exactly-once semantics Kafka can provide in that case. 0") Using a Kafka consumer in order for a message to be consumed by exactly once semantics. 0") Kafka streams exactly once processing use case.

results.content: # exactly once semantics in Kafka source connector. After reading about Kafka idempotent operation and the transactions I wanted to see if Kafka source connectors use any of them in order to ensure exactly-once semantics. After A little bit of reading, I found out that the source connector uses some kind of "offset" of is own which let it store the last operation it did, And then I saw that the Debezium source connector for MongoDB can only achieve at least once semantics. So my question is why can't the MongoDB source connector guarantee exactly-once semantics? if the connector can commit its offset alongside every message with a transaction it can ensure that both the message and the offset are inside Kafka for sure and thus guaranteeing exactly-once semantics. See KIP-618 for source connectors, and 318 to make the producer of connectors idempotent. If the source connector dies between producing the event and committing the offset as part of normal consumer operations, then there's a potential that the consumer will need to reset back to the last uncommitted offset. answered Jan 17, 2020 at 11:42. But this article mentions transactions in Kafka that let you send a batch of messages that all go thru or all fail, which let let you solve the problem if crashing between the committing the event and committing the offset.(correct my if I am wrong). Kafka Connect does not implement the transactional producer.
